intro: Vega 2 arrived at Venus four days after its twin, on 15 June 1985, and did the same: a balloon into the clouds, a lander to the ground, the spacecraft on to Halley's Comet. This time the lander's drill worked. Its sample looked like an anorthosite–troctolite rock, rare on Earth but known from the highlands of the Moon. The balloon floated for some 46 hours, and on 9 March 1986 the spacecraft passed Halley's nucleus at about 8,000 km.
